1	<!-- The standing brief of the skill writer: a headless Claude session that edits the project skills, started fresh by `tools/skill-writer.sh` and resumed for each writing task. Written 2026-10-08 from the first writer's brief, without its first task. -->
2	
3	# The skill writer's standing brief
4	
5	You are the writer for the project skills of the Fortress revival repository, `/home/user/fortress`. The skills are under `.claude/skills/`.
6	
7	The coordinating session briefs you. It resumes this session for each writing task. Keep this brief in mind after a task ends. You are not the coordinating session: do not follow the boot order in `CLAUDE.md`, and do not read `FACTS.md`, `POSITIONS.md` or `INDEX.md` unless a task names an entry.
8	
9	The curator is the person who directs this restoration. The curator reads the skills on a phone, cold, without the project's records in mind. Every agent that works in the repository reads them in the same way.
10	
11	# Your standing order
12	
13	These rules hold for every task.
14	
15	## 1. Write in ASD-STE100, at least halfway
16	
17	ASD-STE100 is Simplified Technical English. It has two kinds of text, and you need both:
18	
19	- **Descriptive text** says what a thing is and how it works. Give the most important information first. Write one topic in each paragraph. Keep each sentence to 25 words or fewer.
20	- **Procedural text** gives steps. Write one instruction in each sentence. Put the condition first: "If X, do Y." Use the imperative. Keep each sentence to 20 words or fewer.
21	
22	Describe first, then give the procedure. A procedure without a description underneath reads like if/else code, and the reader cannot hold it in mind.
23	
24	More rules:
25	
26	- Define a term before you use it. After that, use the same word for the same thing every time. Do not use two words for one thing, or one word for two things.
27	- Define a term in the skill's glossary only if it recurs with one meaning. Elsewhere, write plain words.
28	- Say what to do. Use "do not" only where no positive instruction says the same thing.
29	- Do not fold a list into a sentence. Use a vertical list.
30	- Keep the small words: "the", "a", "that". Do not write in telegraphic shorthand.
31	- Do not write a rule that changes nothing, such as a rule to follow the brief.
32	- A rewrite of existing text is never longer than the text it replaces. New content that a task asks for is the exception.
33	
34	Example. Bad: "Name the way that changes nothing." Good: "Tell which solution keeps the current behaviour."
35	
36	## 2. The glossary form
37	
38	A skill's terms open the skill, in `SKILL.md`, as a definition list with no heading. Each term is bold on its own line. The definition follows on the next line, after ": ". It opens with a noun phrase. Write the term and that noun phrase as a dictionary does, with no article: "revival", not "the revival"; "Person in charge of this restoration", not "The person in charge". The curator chose this form. `fortress-repo`'s `SKILL.md` is the model.
39	
40	## 3. Do not take the register of what you read
41	
42	`explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md`, `POSITIONS.md`, the batch records and many notes were written by earlier models. They use dense agent shorthand: long sentences with many clauses, invented phrases, and terms that only make sense with the whole record in mind. Read them for their content only. Do not copy their wording or their style. Before you keep a sentence, ask: can a reader who is new to the repository understand this sentence without the record?
43	
44	## 4. The principles
45	
46	`explorations/reviews/skills-writing-principles.md` gives the seven principles by which the curator wants a skill written, each with its reason and a pair of texts: one he marked, and the one he accepted. Read it before your first edit. Apply it to every sentence that you write or keep.
47	
48	## 5. How you work
49	
50	- Edit the skill files in place. Git keeps the earlier text.
51	- A comment of the curator marks a problem area. Fix it at the level of its paragraph or section, with the whole skill in mind.
52	- Commit only the paths that you wrote: `git add -- <paths> && git commit -m '<message>' -- <paths>`. End every commit message with these two lines, exactly:
53	
54	      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
55	      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB
56	
57	- Do not push. The coordinator pushes.
58	- Do not touch the review page or its scratch files. The coordinator keeps the page in step.
59	- Provenance goes only in the skill's `references/sources.md`: one line per change. Name its source exactly: the curator's comment and its date, a POSITIONS entry by its title, or "settled by the coordinator". Do not attribute to the curator a choice that the coordinator made.
60	- A part states each rule as the tree holds it. Name no question, item, batch, rung or record file as its source, and give no decision's status (who decided, answered, pending, default). When the curator answers a question, change a part only if the tree changes. In `sources.md`, write provenance as dated history, never as current status.
61	- Before each commit, run `python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/skills-lint.py` on the files you changed. Remove every hit, or say in your report why a hit is a rule.
62	- Do not change what a rule means unless the task asks for it. If a change of meaning seems right, do not make it. List it in your report as a decision not taken, with its alternatives.
63	- Check a claim about the code against the code before you write it. If the task's reason for a change is wrong, say so in your report.
64	- Do not write a model identifier string anywhere. Name models by tier.
65	- Use `git grep`, not `grep -r`.
66	
67	## 6. Your report

70	
71	- the commits, with their hashes;
72	- the new text of each changed sentence, or for a larger change, each file's size before and after and what changed;
73	- the decisions not taken, each with its alternatives;
74	- anything in the task that you could not follow, and why.

<!-- The clarity workflow: rewrite POSITIONS or FACTS entries so that each reads on its own, with a cold read and a fidelity check, as a Workflow run; how to run it and what to do with its output. -->

# The clarity workflow

`record-clarity.js` rewrites record entries so that a reader who knows the language, but never saw the conversation or the batch behind an entry, can tell what it says. It is the process of the clarity pilot of 2026-10-22 (`positions-audit/clarity/`, ten POSITIONS entries, approved and applied at `6b560762f`), run as a Workflow, in the shape of the `fortress-repo` skill rewrite of 2026-10-08 (Workflow run `wf_185878c8-0fb`: writers, cold readers, a fix round). Its standard is Astra's review, `explorations/reviews/revival-record-synthesis.md`.

## What runs, for each chunk of about ten entries

1. **Assess** (FACTS only): Astra's rubric over every entry (`assess.md`); a disposition each: keep, reword, reorganize or investigate. Only reword and reorganize go on.
2. **Write**: an Opus writer with the skill writer's standing brief and `writer.md`. For POSITIONS its evidence is the provenance audit's, by `entries.py`; for FACTS, the assessment and each entry's cited sources.
3. **Cold read**: an Opus reader with only the `fortress-repo` skill's core and area parts, never its revival part (`coldread.md`).
4. **Check**: fidelity against the sources, and the reader's answers against the source meaning (`check.md`).
5. **Fix**: the writer's second round (`fix.md`).
6. **Reread**: a second cold read of the fixed entries.

All agents are Opus. A Workflow runs at most two agents at once on this machine: run several side by side.

## Running it

    Workflow({ scriptPath: '/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/record-clarity.js',
               args: { kind: 'positions' | 'facts', out: '/abs/folder/', chunks: [{ name: 'c1', entries: ['P-7', 'P-8'] }] } })

Each chunk's files land in `out` + its name: `proposals.md`, `clean.txt`, `proposals.apply`, `concepts.md`, `cold-read.md`, `check.md`, `cold-read-2.md`, and for FACTS `assessment.md`. Resume a killed run with the same script path, `resumeFromRunId` and the same args, byte for byte.

## After a chunk

The coordinator reads `proposals.md` and `cold-read-2.md`, then:
- applies `proposals.apply` on a copy of the record and runs `record.py check --base`, then on `main`, and commits the record with the chunk's files;
- files each question for the curator, and each "investigate" entry's question, in `review-queue.md`; a change of meaning that no source settles is not applied;
- merges `concepts.md` into the list for the worker skill's orientation.

POSITIONS entries need the provenance audit's evidence first: for entries it has not traced, run the mining workflow (`positions-audit/README.md`).
14:## What an entry is
15-
16-An entry lets a worker or you act right without opening the report, and says when the report is needed. Its number is permanent and never reused. Its title and text are rewritten freely, since the number is the key.
17-
18-- A FACTS entry holds, after its number and a bold title that states the fact: the fact as it stands now; what it means for the work, such as what it blocks or which row or decision it bears on; the test that gates it, or its source; the decision it builds, by number; and the report section that holds the detail.
19-- A POSITIONS entry holds, after its number and a bold title: what the curator decided about the project, and why, in one or two sentences; what it means for the work; and what is still to build, with its PLAN item. It lists no FACTS entries: `P-48+` finds them.
20-- Quote the curator only where the exact words are the decision. Otherwise condense the words into the position, keeping the part of the rule that cuts. Check the condensed text against the words before you write it. The dictated words go to the history, with their time.
21-- A count that each landing changes has one entry with its current value, what it counts, the kinds with the largest share, and how to read a move. Other entries give its number. A count from one measurement says so.
22-- An entry holds one claim that can be kept up to date on its own, with its conditions, exceptions and evidence. Split an entry when its claims answer different questions and change apart. Before you split, look for an entry that already holds the claim, and move the text there. After a split, grep the record for the old number, and repoint each pointer that meant the claim that moved.
23-- If several entries together establish a conclusion that workers keep working out again, make it a sentence of the entry that owns its subject, with pointers to the entries it rests on. The pass updates it when one of them changes. Add a new entry only if no entry owns it. Leave a conclusion nobody has checked in its report, out of the entries.
24-- Keep an entry near 600 characters. This is a check, not a cap, and no reason to split: an entry may pass it if a question below keeps a sentence.
25-- Write halfway to ASD-STE100.
26-
27-Ask of each sentence, and act on the answer:
28-
29-1. Would the reader do otherwise without it? Keep it.
30-2. Would the reader misread another sentence without it? Keep it.
31-3. Does it tell how the fact came about: a date, a batch, a correction? Move it to the history.
32-4. Is it detail needed only while doing the work: a line number, a list of sites, a timing? Leave it in the report, and name the section.
33-5. Does another entry or a skill say it? Give that entry's number, or the skill's part.
34-6. Can a reader new to the project follow every word? Name the kind of each count.
35-
36-Before you write or check the first entries of a consolidation, read the five worked examples: `facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/record-rule-draft.md#Worked examples'`, a large read.
37-
38-## Reading and writing
39-
40-- `git log -S'F-87' --oneline -- explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md` lists the commits that touched an entry.
41-- To read a history in depth, or a report's passage, send a Sonnet scout. The provenance lines tell it where to dig.
42-- `record.py`'s header gives its usage. `add`, `set`, `merge`, `remove` and `apply` write; each needs `--from PATH#HEADING` or `--note WHY`. The tool stamps the time and copies the earlier line to the history.
43-- Before every commit, run `record.py check --base <the commit before your edits>`. It shows that nothing was lost, and reports each entry over 600 characters.
44-- Commit the record file and its history together.

## P45: fidelity and comprehensibility are separate checks

On October 22 the curator supplied a screenshot and copied text of a proposed P-45 revision from the positions audit. The artifact URL could not be retrieved; this review concerns the supplied example, not the entire list. The screenshot distinguishes deletions from retained text; the copied text alone mixes both. The original ruling and its provenance have not been re-audited here.

**Finding:** removing historical material improves the entry but does not by itself make the remaining decision understandable. The difficulty is visible in the formulation, not necessarily a lack of Fortress knowledge on the reader's part.

- It mixes requirements with statements of implementation behaviour. “The checker runs” and “walk and the checker accept the same pairs” read as established facts, while “Still to build” points to remaining disagreements. State clearly whether agreement is a requirement or an achieved result.
- “No parameter pair required to exclude”, “refused families” and “reads otherwise” conceal important meaning in compressed technical wording. Name the objects and the operation precisely.
- “The paper's three overloading rules” neither identifies the paper precisely nor states enough of the decision to orient the reader. A reference may supply detail; it should not replace the explanation of what was decided.
- “No model line changes” compresses a consequential constraint into project shorthand. Identify the microGPT model program and state the exact restriction established by the ruling.
- A tracked diff makes historical and current wording compete for attention. Show the clean proposed entry first, with the diff available underneath.

### Proposed form, subject to checking the ruling

Lead with the decision. Follow with its essential scope, reason and exact technical conditions. Distinguish any remaining implementation work and point to its proper record. Preserve conditions that limit the decision; do not simplify away those conditions merely to improve fluency.

An illustrative opening is:

> **P-45 — Use the 2011 overloading model in the specification and both execution paths.** Allow overloads whose static parameters differ. The compiler's checker and the interpreter must apply the same rules when deciding which overload declarations are permitted.

This is a presentation example, **not a verified replacement for P45**. It must be checked against the curator's actual ruling before adoption, and it does not replace the technical requirements omitted from this short opening. In the final entry, identify the 2011 source precisely. Do not turn an implementation default or a writer's inference into the curator's decision.

### Two checks in the existing rewrite process

1. **Fidelity:** compare the proposed entry with the recorded ruling and its qualifications. Distinguish the curator's words from the coordinator's interpretation, an implementation choice and a fact about the current tree. Keep the provenance in history.
2. **Comprehensibility:** give a cold reader the clean entry and its declared prerequisite context, without the original discussion. Ask it to paraphrase what the curator decided, where it applies, what it requires, and what remains unfinished. Compare that paraphrase with the source-backed meaning. If the reader has to reconstruct the original discussion to resolve the wording, revise the entry.

The acceptance question is:

> Can a reader distinguish what Pavol decided, what the implementation currently does, and what remains unfinished?

A citation establishes where a statement came from; it does not establish that the statement communicates its meaning. This check does not require a type-theory lesson inside every position. It requires enough context to identify the decision before following pointers for technical detail.

This is a proposed improvement to positions writing, distinct from Revival's admission rule. A ruling remains part of POSITIONS even when a worker would already agree with it by default. No POSITIONS entry, skill or audit proposal was edited here.

## For Fable: rewrite positions before consolidating Revival

**Current priority, requested by the curator on October 22:** finish the faithful, readable rewriting of POSITIONS before consolidating the skill's Revival part. This section is the starting brief for that work; the rest of this report supplies background. It does not authorize changing a ruling or treating a proposed wording as an approved decision.

### Reader and register

Assume the reader knows the relevant language concepts, or can reach their definitions through the normal skill references, but does not remember the conversation that produced the decision. A position must communicate the ruling without requiring that conversation.

Apply the project's existing **ASD-STE100-inspired register (“halfway”)** to these entries, not only to skills. Read:

- `explorations/coordinator/skill-writer-brief.md`, section 1, for the writing guidance.
- `explorations/reviews/skills-writing-principles.md`, for the worked examples and principles.
- `.claude/skills/coordinator/references/record.md`, for entry ownership, scope, history and the record-writing procedure.

These are writing references, not a request to adopt unrelated skill-writer duties. Use familiar verbs, explicit subjects and antecedents, consistent technical terms, and one main point per sentence. Put the condition before the action when that makes the rule easier to follow. Separate a decision from its reason and implementation status. Short sentences must preserve qualifications; do not meet a word target by replacing precise meaning with shorthand.

The curator suspects that older entries predate this register and have not received a comparable prose pass. That chronology has not been established entry by entry. The observed wording defects justify the clarity pass regardless of their age. This is an adaptation of ASD-STE100 guidance, not a claim of formal compliance.

### What the supplied examples show

The P45, P50 and P51 reviews are based on the curator's pasted text and screenshots of proposed edits, not a fresh verification of the original rulings.

**P45 needs structural clarification.** Separate what the curator requires from claims about achieved behaviour. Lead with the decision; retain exact technical restrictions; put detailed implementation gaps in their existing record homes, with a concise pointer where needed. The illustrative opening in the preceding P45 section remains provisional.

**P50 and P51 need a smaller clarity pass.** Each already centres on a recognizable rule. Removing the historical material is useful; do not require a wholesale rewrite merely because the reader needs language knowledge.

For P50:

- Replace the grammatical compression “its exits' with values” with wording that explicitly identifies the values supplied by exits.
- “P-51 is the other half of item 48” describes the old discussion's organization. State the substantive relationship if it helps the reader; otherwise leave that association in history.
- Expected-type propagation into the label body and its exits is the central decision. Keep its scope intact. Verify any proposed restatement against the ruling rather than inferring further type-theoretical claims from it.

For P51:

- “When the checker's attempts at a call keep none” should identify exactly what the initial check failed to find. “If the initial check finds no applicable overload” is a possible wording **only if it matches the recorded trigger**.
- Distinguish the outer call from the inner call used as its argument. Repeated uses of “call” should not force the reader to infer which one is meant.
- Preserve the boundary “any inferred static argument, not only a result-only type parameter”. This affects which cases the decision covers.
- Replace “it makes the inference rules one rule everywhere” with the particular consistency the ruling sought. Do not widen the decision or invent a stronger rationale.
- The probe's measurement belongs in its report. A short implementation-status statement can remain if it accurately reports the relevant completion; it must not imply that every related gap is closed.

### A bounded rewrite and check

For each entry already under review:

1. Recover the ruling and its qualifications from the provenance gathered by the current audit. Distinguish the curator's decision from a coordinator default, a worker choice and an implementation fact.
2. Write the clean proposed entry in the register above. Preserve the permanent identifier. Keep decision, scope and essential reason together. Retain technical conditions that affect what is allowed.
3. Check fidelity against the source, including whether the rewrite makes the claim stronger or broader. Keep historical wording and provenance in the established history mechanism.
4. Check comprehension with the normal prerequisite context but without the original discussion. Ask the reader to restate the decision, its trigger and limits, and any unfinished work.
5. Classify a failure before fixing it: missing language concept, unclear wording, or uncertain fidelity. Supply or link a definition for the first; rewrite the second; return to the evidence or curator for the third.
6. Present the clean proposal first and its diff underneath for the curator's review. Apply approved edits through the existing record tooling and preserve their history.

This refines the existing fidelity and cold-reader checks; it does not require a new large audit or a separate agent for every entry. Focus review effort on changed or ambiguous decisions.

**Acceptance question:** can a reader with the normal language prerequisites explain what Pavol decided and where it applies, without reconstructing the original conversation?

Do not inflate Revival to supply all those prerequisites. Ordinary language concepts belong in the core or appropriate area reference. Revival retains its narrower role of correcting mistaken assumptions about revived Fortress. Nor should a ruling be removed from POSITIONS merely because it matches a worker's default belief: the per-entry necessity test for Revival is not a deletion rule for the curator's decisions.

No POSITIONS entries or skill files were changed by this report update.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

It is often desirable to know that a value lies in a subset of its type,
such as the positive values, the nonzero values, or the finite values.

content.content:
\EXP{\TYP{Just}(v)} declared as follows:
%(* Optional Values *)
%trait Maybe[\T\] comprises { Nothing[\T\], Just[\T\] }
%  isNothing: Boolean
%end
%value object Nothing[\T\] extends Maybe[\T\]
%end
%object Just[\T\](just: T) extends Maybe[\T\]
%end
\begin{Fortress}
\(\mathtt{(*}\;\hbox{\rm  Optional Values \unskip}\;\mathtt{*)}\)\\
\(\KWD{trait}\:\TYP{Maybe}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket \KWD{comprises} \{\,\TYP{Nothing}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket, \TYP{Just}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket\,\}\)\\
{\tt~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(  \VAR{isNothing}\COLON \TYP{Boolean}\)\-\\\poptabs
\(\KWD{end}\)\\
\(\KWD{value}\;\;\KWD{object}\:\TYP{Nothing}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket \KWD{extends}\:\TYP{Maybe}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket\)\\
\(\KWD{end}\)\\
\(\KWD{object}\:\TYP{Just}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket(\VAR{just}\COLON T) \KWD{extends}\:\TYP{Maybe}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket\)\\
\(\KWD{end}\)
\end{Fortress}
The empty case is one object for each type \VAR{T},
and each use writes the type,
as in \EXP{\TYP{Nothing}\llbracket\TYP{String}\rrbracket}.
The following declaration of a single \TYP{Nothing} for every
instantiation of \TYP{Maybe} is not allowed:
%(* Not allowed! *)
%object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}
%end
\begin{Fortress}
\(\mathtt{(*}\;\hbox{\rm  Not allowed! \unskip}\;\mathtt{*)}\)\\
\(\KWD{object} \TYP{Nothing} \KWD{extends} \TYP{Maybe}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket \KWD{excludes} \TYP{Just}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket \KWD{where} \{T \KWD{extends} \TYP{Object}\}\)\\
\(\KWD{end}\)
\end{Fortress}
It would make \TYP{Nothing} a \EXP{\TYP{Maybe}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket}
for every \VAR{T} at once,
which instantiation exclusion forbids (\secref{where-clauses});
and an object declaration has no \KWD{excludes} clause
(\secref{object-decls}), an object trait type already excluding
every type that is not its supertype (\secref{object-traits}).
\revision{revival-nothing}{The Working Draft of February 2011 declared
\TYP{Nothing} with the declaration marked ``Not allowed''.

An apply file holds, in any order: `## TITLE` or `### TITLE`, the section the
new entries below it go to (an existing entry stands under no heading, or
under its own section's, or the `## ` one that holds it); entry lines as they
should stand, `- F-87 ...`, or `- F-?1 ...` for a new entry, its placeholder
replaced by its number everywhere in the file; `move F-87 to SECTION`;
`remove F-90`; `merge F-91 into F-87`; `note F-87`, or `note F-87 correcting
TIME`, a noted block. Each may be followed by one indented provenance line of
its own:
`  from: PATH, "HEADING"; commit: HASH; by: WHO; note: WHY`. Blank lines and
`<!-- -->` comments are ignored. An entry line equal to the entry is skipped:
to add to its history, write `note F-87`. A note whose block the history holds
already, all but its time, is skipped too, so a file run twice writes nothing
twice. One call writes one block per entry, so an entry is noted, or changed,
once in a file.

check fails on: an entry line without its number, or a line under an entry
that continues it; a number on two lines; a number with no `numbered` or
`added` block, or one gone from its file whose last block is not `merged into`
or `removed`; a noted block that holds an earlier line, or whose `correcting`
names no earlier block of its entry, or more than one; a pointer to no live
entry, or quoted words that do not open the target's title; with --base, an
entry at COMMIT that is neither its line now nor the earlier line of a block
in its history (pointer words refreshed by the tool aside). It reports, without failing: the entries over 600 characters, the
entries without a bold title, and the `--from` paths and the report sections
an entry cites (`PATH`, "HEADING") that do not resolve.
